text: 🇲🇽🎨 "In 2026, the world's democracies are starting to say: enough — not with our children." "The companies that control our children's attention used algorithms and AI to hook every child, in order to sell their attention. Then they lied about it." — Jonathan Haidt, NYU psychologist, author of The Anxious Generation Haidt addressed Mexico's mañanera by video — in Spanish — and urged two measures: phone-free schools (already in 25 US states) and 16 as the minimum age for social media accounts, following Australia's lead.

🇲🇽✊ Ñuu Tata — "the town that cares." Oaxaca is getting a three-hospital health city with 700+ beds. "In Mixtec they named it 'Ñuu Tata,' which means 'town that cares.' Three hospitals — ISSSTE, IMSS, and IMSS Bienestar — sharing services, more than 700 beds. For the first time, conceived as the Universal Health Service." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, after her weekend tour of Oaxaca The regional health city will serve all of Oaxaca and part of Puebla, with next-generation technology and every specialty. Yesterday the first stone was laid for the IMSS regional hospital in San Lorenzo Cacaotepec.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico's scholarship system: 19.6 million students. 93.7 billion pesos in the first half of 2026 alone. "If one student stays in school, a family wins. But if millions of students stay in school, the entire nation wins." — Julio León Trujillo, National Scholarship Coordinator Coverage: 14.96M in basic education, 4.16M in high school, 470K university scholarships. 2026 target: 22 million students — the largest scholarship system in the country's history. The Gertrudis Bocanegra transport scholarship expands to Zacatecas and Chiapas next cycle.

🇲🇽✊ Starting today: 6.7 million primary school students receive 2,500 pesos for supplies and uniforms. "What was promised is delivered. The President said the school-supply support would go out in August — today the dispersal of the 2,500 pesos begins." — Julio León Trujillo, National Scholarship Coordinator Deposits run August 3–14, staggered by last-name initial: 16.7 billion pesos to 6,694,988 students. 4.7 million Bienestar cards delivered (95.1%); the rest go office-by-office and door-to-door — one card was delivered to a mother who was in labor during delivery week.

🇲🇽💵 <u>REMITTANCES TO MEXICO UP 3.1% IN FIRST HALF OF 2026</u>

Remittances to Mexico reached $30.759 billion in January-June, up 3.1% year-on-year and rising for a fifth consecutive month, Banxico reported — 13 million transactions averaging $422 each (El Financiero).

Trump slapped a tax on remittances and promised mass deportations. The money Mexican families depend on keeps flowing anyway.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>PLAN KUKULKÁN: THE OPERATION THAT SECURED THE WORLD CUP</u>

Baja California is joining Plan Kukulkán, the strategy that protected the 2026 World Cup, as Governor Marina del Pilar recognized the operation that coordinated more than 124,000 federal, state and municipal personnel.

Mexico hosted the planet's biggest sporting event without a major incident — and showed, in President Sheinbaum's words, "the true face of Mexico: a country at peace and joyful."

🇲🇽🐝 <u>SUPREME COURT TAKES UP CASE TO RECOGNIZE BEES AS RIGHTS HOLDERS</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court will hear a case brought by Maya communities of Hopelchén, Campeche, seeking recognition of bees as subjects of rights after years of mass die-offs linked to fipronil and neonicotinoid pesticides.

For the Maya people, the justices heard, bees are "part of a biocultural heritage built over centuries" — tied to traditional beekeeping, food, ritual and identity.

A ruling could set precedent on the rights of nature, aerial spraying and endangered-species status for the melipona bee.

🇲🇽🏫 <u>RECORD 58.4 BILLION PESOS FOR MEXICO'S SCHOOLS</u>

The federal government will invest 58,415 million pesos in school infrastructure in 2026 — the largest federal outlay ever for Mexico's classrooms, not counting what the states spend.

Through La Escuela es Nuestra alone, 71,482 schools have been rehabilitated this year, prioritized by marginalization. Add 31 new high schools, 156,240 new student places and a projected 22 million scholarship recipients by year-end.

"A historic investment for the country's schools," President Sheinbaum said.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S COMPUTER EXPORTS TO THE US JUMP 72.6%</u>

Mexican exports of computer equipment to the United States hit $52 billion in January-May, up 72.64% year-on-year — now 35% of everything the US buys from Mexico, ahead of cars.

T-MEC compliance in the sector went from 0% to 91.5% in a year as companies retooled for the preferential tariff; the effective tariff paid in May was 0.01%. Mexico is now the second-largest computer supplier to the US, with 33.7% of the market.

The AI boom runs through Mexican assembly lines.

🇲🇽⚓ <u>MEXICO'S NAVY SEIZES 4.4 TONS OF COCAINE OFF OAXACA AND CHIAPAS</u>

Mexico's Navy intercepted three boats off the coasts of Oaxaca and Chiapas and seized 4.4 tons of cocaine, detaining 16 people — 127 packages and 42 bricks in the first action alone, plus 2,000 liters of fuel in the second.

"In this administration, the Navy has secured more than 80 tons of cocaine in Mexican seas," Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch reported.

No foreign boots, no lectures. Mexican forces, Mexican waters, Mexican results.
